items.stem: Which of the following best describes "laogai"?
options: The Protestant group formed in 1934 by pastors such as Martin Niemöller and Dietrich Bonhoeffer to resist Nazi control of the Church
The Nazi organisation under Robert Ley that replaced trade unions after they were abolished on 2 May 1933
The body set up by Goebbels in September 1933 that every writer, artist, musician and journalist had to join
The Chinese system of forced labour camps, meaning “reform through labour”
items.answer: The Chinese system of forced labour camps, meaning “reform through labour”
items.markingKey: D. "laogai" is the Chinese system of forced labour camps, meaning “reform through labour”.

items.stem: Distinguish between the use of terror in Fascist Italy and the use of terror in Nazi Germany.
items.answer: Nazi terror was large-scale, run by the SS and Gestapo with concentration camps and genocide; Fascist terror was more limited, relying on confino (internal exile), the OVRA and a special tribunal, with relatively few executions.
items.markingKey: Nazi terror was large-scale, run by the SS and Gestapo with concentration camps and genocide; Fascist terror was more limited, relying on confino (internal exile), the OVRA and a special tribunal, with relatively few executions. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: A student claims that terror in Nazi Germany was directed equally at all Germans. Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Terror targeted specific groups – communists, socialists, Jews, Roma, homosexuals, “asocials” – while most conformist Germans had little contact with the Gestapo.
items.markingKey: Terror targeted specific groups – communists, socialists, Jews, Roma, homosexuals, “asocials” – while most conformist Germans had little contact with the Gestapo. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Briefly describe the Night of the Long Knives (30 June – 2 July 1934) and explain what it reveals about the use of terror to consolidate power.
items.answer: The SS murdered Ernst Röhm, other SA leaders and opponents such as Kurt von Schleicher; about 85–200 were killed. It removed the SA as a rival to the army, won army support for Hitler as head of state, and showed that the regime would kill to protect itself.
items.markingKey: Context (The SS murdered Ernst Röhm, other SA leaders and opponents such as Kurt von Schleicher; about 85–200 were killed.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. The Gestapo was not an omnipresent organisation. The office in Würzburg, responsible for the whole of Lower Franconia, had only a couple of dozen officials. Its success depended on the willingness of citizens to inform on their neighbours.

In what ways do Sources A and B agree and disagree about the use of terror and repression in authoritarian states?
items.answer: Both concern how regimes treated critics. Mao’s speech appears to invite free debate, while Gellately shows Nazi control relied on citizens denouncing neighbours; A suggests openness (later reversed), B shows the social basis of repression.

items.stem: "Authoritarian regimes were successful in controlling education and the arts." Discuss.
items.answer: Regimes achieved extensive formal control, but private beliefs and cultural life were harder to control.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: Reich Chamber of Culture and Gleichschaltung; Hitler Youth compulsory from 1936/1939; model operas and Cultural Revolution. Arguments against: Church schools in Italy; nonconformist youth groups; private indifference and humour; intellectual emigration. Supported judgement: Regimes achieved extensive formal control, but private beliefs and cultural life were harder to control. items.stem:
Source A: Martin Niemöller, German Protestant pastor, words from his post-war lectures, c. 1946 (widely quoted version)

First they came for the socialists, and I did not speak out – because I was not a socialist. Then they came for the trade unionists, and I did not speak out – because I was not a trade unionist. Then they came for me – and there was no one left to speak for me.

Source B: Paraphrased from Robert Ley, leader of the German Labour Front, speech of May 1933

The trade unions are dead. In their place stands the German Labour Front, which embraces employer and worker alike. The class struggle is over.

In what ways do Sources A and B agree and disagree about the treatment of opposition in authoritarian states?
items.answer: Both refer to the destruction of the trade unions. Niemöller sees it as one stage in the elimination of all opposition and laments the failure to resist, while Ley celebrates it as the end of class struggle; A is a critical reflection, B regime propaganda.

items.stem: Define the term "Gestapo".
items.answer: The Nazi secret state police, created in Prussia by Göring in 1933 and later controlled by Himmler and Heydrich
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: the Nazi secret state police, created in Prussia by Göring in 1933 and later controlled by Himmler and Heydrich. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: State what is meant by the term "Degenerate Art exhibition".
items.answer: The Nazi exhibition in Munich in 1937 that ridiculed modern art as “un-German”
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: the Nazi exhibition in Munich in 1937 that ridiculed modern art as “un-German”. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Explain the difference between resistance and nonconformity.
items.answer: Resistance means active attempts to undermine or overthrow the regime (e.g. the July Plot of 1944); nonconformity means refusing to conform in limited ways, such as telling jokes or listening to banned music.
items.markingKey: Resistance means active attempts to undermine or overthrow the regime (e.g. the July Plot of 1944); nonconformity means refusing to conform in limited ways, such as telling jokes or listening to banned music. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain the difference between foreign policy driven by ideology and foreign policy as a tool of domestic consolidation.
items.answer: Foreign policy can be used to win popularity and unity at home; ideologically driven policy pursues aims such as Lebensraum regardless of domestic effects.
items.markingKey: Foreign policy can be used to win popularity and unity at home; ideologically driven policy pursues aims such as Lebensraum regardless of domestic effects. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain why terror was combined with propaganda in authoritarian states.
items.answer: Terror deterred opposition but could not create enthusiasm; propaganda sought genuine consent, so the two together maintained power.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Terror deterred opposition but could not create enthusiasm; propaganda sought genuine consent, so the two together maintained power. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain the difference between control of the arts in Nazi Germany and control of the arts in Mao’s China.
items.answer: Both demanded political conformity, but Nazi culture promoted racial and völkisch themes through the Chamber of Culture, while Maoist culture promoted class struggle; under the Cultural Revolution only eight “model operas” were permitted.
items.markingKey: Both demanded political conformity, but Nazi culture promoted racial and völkisch themes through the Chamber of Culture, while Maoist culture promoted class struggle; under the Cultural Revolution only eight “model operas” were permitted. items.stem: Explain why opposition to the Nazi regime was so limited.
items.answer: Terror, the destruction of parties and unions, propaganda, economic recovery and the popularity of Hitler isolated opponents, while the left was divided and the elites largely collaborated.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Terror, the destruction of parties and unions, propaganda, economic recovery and the popularity of Hitler isolated opponents, while the left was divided and the elites largely collaborated. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: With reference to the Bay of Pigs invasion (April 1961), explain how it illustrates the use of external threat to consolidate power.
items.answer: Castro’s forces defeated about 1,400 CIA-trained Cuban exiles within three days. Victory boosted Castro’s prestige, allowed mass arrests of suspected opponents and led him to declare the revolution socialist.
items.markingKey: Context (Castro’s forces defeated about 1,400 CIA-trained Cuban exiles within three days.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.answer: Nazi youth control was incomplete; compulsion caused boredom and some young people formed nonconformist groups.

items.stem: With reference to the purge of Peng Dehuai at the Lushan Conference (July–August 1959), explain how it illustrates the treatment of opposition within the ruling party.
items.answer: Peng criticised the Great Leap Forward in a private letter; Mao circulated it and denounced him as leader of an “anti-party clique”. It deterred honest reporting of the famine and showed that even senior leaders could not criticise Mao.

items.stem: Outline one way in which the Abyssinian War (1935–1936) shows the use of foreign policy to strengthen the regime.
items.answer: Italy used poison gas and conquered Ethiopia; Mussolini proclaimed an empire in May 1936. Victory over League sanctions produced a peak of popularity for Mussolini, though it drew him closer to Hitler.

items.stem: "Authoritarian regimes dealt with opposition mainly through repression." Discuss.
items.answer: Repression was central, but regimes also used compromise and incentives to neutralise opponents.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: banning parties and unions; imprisonment of Niemöller; purge of Peng Dehuai. Arguments against: Concordat and Lateran Pacts as compromise; DAF benefits like Strength through Joy; propaganda and consent.
